data.claim: Growth hormone / IGF-1 axis inhibits Longevity
data.mechanism: Growth hormone / IGF-1 signalling acts as a brake on lifespan: mice whose GH signalling is blocked, either lifelong or from middle age, live longer and are less frail in old age.
data.mechanism_beginner: Less growth-hormone signalling, longer life in mice.
data.boundary: Mouse only. A lifelong GH-receptor-antagonist transgenic (LIST2026; an earlier study of the same line did not detect extension) and a tamoxifen-inducible whole-body Ghr knockout started at 12 months (DUR2026). mTOR signalling was not measured in either, so the route through PI3K-Akt-mTOR is inferred, not shown here.
data.note: 2026-10-10: Interaction type signal-relay -> functional-consequence. The target is a lifespan outcome, not a signalling node, and mTOR signalling was not measured in either study.
